No other independently violable obligation (containment, endpoint, trigger, guard, effect, action, reachability, event-consumer, termination) is established by NL1-NL3 beyond what the primary plan already covers: NL2's initial_entry and trigger_set contracts capture activation and trigger obligations, and NL3's containment, region_structure, and state_action contracts capture the orthogonal-region and concurrent-operation obligations. No termination, guard-disjointness, event-consumer-coverage, or variable-delta obligation is explicitly established by this NL closure beyond what is already present.

additional_contracts.normative_statement: Each collision-avoidance control sub-region (RearEnd, Pedestrian) owned by the active collision-avoidance mode must have its own valid owner-local default entry into a child state within that same owner scope, so that the control can actually operate as part of the required concurrent/orthogonal structure.
additional_contracts.quote: The orthogonal regions of the active mode of collision avoidance allow for concurrent activation different of collision avoidance controls.
additional_contracts.reason: NL3 requires the active collision-avoidance mode's regions to support concurrent activation of distinct collision-avoidance controls (Frontend, RearEnd, Pedestrian). response.reason: This lens compares NL contracts NL2 (sub-machine activation/initial entry and trigger set), NL3 (containment/region-structure/state-action), and the cardinality contracts against the exact source inventory, canonical PlantUML, working-contract macro mapping, and closed FCSTM/inspection-equivalent facts. The source inventory and PlantUML show three sibling composites (Frontend, RearEnd, Pedestrian) under CollisionAvoidanceSystem, each with a local [*] -> Idle-style initial edge, but the source-inventory RearEnd/Pedestrian initial edges target 'CollisionAvoidanceSystem.Frontend.Idle', an out-of-owner target, and the closed FCSTM realizes this as synthetic InvalidInitialtr_0005/InvalidInitialtr_0009 placeholder states that are permanently unreachable and never enter the collision-avoidance behavior. No entering transition on CollisionAvoidanceSystem is triggered by any of the three collision-detection events; the only inbound edge is an unconditional root initial edge, and the model does not implement the disjunctive event-based activation NL2 requires. Region containment (NL3) is not established as concurrent/orthogonal in the closed model: CollisionAvoidanceSystem is a single ordinary composite with three sequential child composites and no declared parallel-region separator, so orthogonal concurrent activation cannot occur, and the state-action concurrency obligation is likewise unsupported. Cardinality contracts are handled via cardinality_bindings only, per protocol.

output.reason: This lens compares NL contracts NL2 (sub-machine activation/initial entry and trigger set), NL3 (containment/region-structure/state-action), and the cardinality contracts against the exact source inventory, canonical PlantUML, working-contract macro mapping, and closed FCSTM/inspection-equivalent facts. The source inventory and PlantUML show three sibling composites (Frontend, RearEnd, Pedestrian) under CollisionAvoidanceSystem, each with a local [*] -> Idle-style initial edge, but the source-inventory RearEnd/Pedestrian initial edges target 'CollisionAvoidanceSystem.Frontend.Idle', an out-of-owner target, and the closed FCSTM realizes this as synthetic InvalidInitialtr_0005/InvalidInitialtr_0009 placeholder states that are permanently unreachable and never enter the collision-avoidance behavior. No entering transition on CollisionAvoidanceSystem is triggered by any of the three collision-detection events; the only inbound edge is an unconditional root initial edge, and the model does not implement the disjunctive event-based activation NL2 requires. Region containment (NL3) is not established as concurrent/orthogonal in the closed model: CollisionAvoidanceSystem is a single ordinary composite with three sequential child composites and no declared parallel-region separator, so orthogonal concurrent activation cannot occur, and the state-action concurrency obligation is likewise unsupported. Cardinality contracts are handled via cardinality_bindings only, per protocol.

issues.reason: NL3 requires the active mode to contain orthogonal regions; the exact canonical/source model records zero concurrent regions and the FCSTM textual structure has no parallel-region separator, so containment of orthogonal regions is missing.

issues.strongest_rebuttal: One could argue the three named sub-machines (Frontend/RearEnd/Pedestrian) are intended as the three concurrent regions even without an explicit separator; but PlantUML/canonical semantics treat a composite with plain nested state blocks and no separator as a single region, so this reading is not structurally supported without an explicit region marker.

issues.basis: canonical_source_ir.model.concurrent_regions.count=0; inspection_equivalent_facts.states showing Frontend/RearEnd/Pedestrian as ordinary nested composites with independent is_composite=true but no region grouping metadata; verify_facts.non_proved reachability=false for RearEnd and Pedestrian precluding concurrent activation.

issues.reason: This is the region_structure obligation distinct from bare containment: it requires the concurrent-activation-enabling structure itself, which the source/model do not provide since there is no parallel-region construct and no concurrent reachability among the three sub-machines.
issues.requirement_quote: The orthogonal regions of the active mode of collision avoidance allow for concurrent activation different of collision avoidance controls.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: A reviewer might treat the mere presence of three separate named composite children as evidence of intended concurrency; but structurally this is one implicit non-parallel region per UML/PlantUML semantics, and no runtime path can activate more than one of the three children concurrently given the unreachable RearEnd/Pedestrian, so the region-structure obligation is unmet.
issues.title: No orthogonal/concurrent region structure exists to enable simultaneous activation of distinct collision avoidance controls

issues.basis: exact_source_inventory.transitions tr_0005 (source=@initial:CollisionAvoidanceSystem.RearEnd, target=CollisionAvoidanceSystem.Frontend.Idle) and tr_0009 (source=@initial:CollisionAvoidanceSystem.Pedestrian, target=CollisionAvoidanceSystem.Frontend.Idle); fcstm_model.text state RearEnd/Pedestrian containing InvalidInitialtr_0005/InvalidInitialtr_0009 named 'PlantUML initial target outside child scope'; inspection_equivalent_facts.states reachable_from_initial:false for RearEnd/Pedestrian/InvalidInitialtr_0005/InvalidInitialtr_0009.
issues.expected: On rear-end or pedestrian collision detection, the exact owning composite (RearEnd or Pedestrian) must be entered/activated with its own valid nested initial edge and a reachable path from the root.
issues.observed: exact_source_inventory shows tr_0005 (@initial:CollisionAvoidanceSystem.RearEnd -> CollisionAvoidanceSystem.Frontend.Idle) and tr_0009 (@initial:CollisionAvoidanceSystem.Pedestrian -> CollisionAvoidanceSystem.Frontend.Idle) both target a state outside their own owner scope (Frontend.Idle instead of a RearEnd/Pedestrian-local child). The closed FCSTM materializes this as synthetic placeholder targets state:InvalidInitialtr_0005 and state:InvalidInitialtr_0009, and neither RearEnd nor Pedestrian is reachable_from_initial in the closed model (inspection_equivalent_facts.states, verify_facts refuted reachability). No transition anywhere is triggered by a 'possible frontend collision', 'rear-end collision', or 'collision with pedestrian' event distinct from the internal 'Collision Detected' event used inside each composite's own Idle->Braking edge, and even that internal trigger is unreachable.
issues.reason: NL2 requires the sub-machine (each of Frontend/RearEnd/Pedestrian, since they structurally realize the three detection scenarios) to be entered/activated on its own detection event. The exact source inventory shows tr_0005 and tr_0009 as malformed nested initial edges whose target lies in a sibling scope (Frontend.Idle) rather than inside RearEnd/Pedestrian, which the FCSTM compiler resolves into synthetic invalid-initial placeholder states with no path back to the root. issues.strongest_rebuttal: An observer could argue tr_0005/tr_0009 exist as PlantUML-authored initial edges and are therefore satisfied declarations; but the malformed out-of-scope target (a different composite's child) and the resulting synthetic InvalidInitial placeholder show the nested initial edge does not validly enter RearEnd/Pedestrian's own scope, and the composite itself is unreachable from root, so activation cannot occur.
issues.title: RearEnd/Pedestrian initial edges target Frontend.Idle outside their own scope, and no owner-local edge activates them from a detection event
